findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted as public with no ACL restricting access, allowing unauthenticated or unauthorized users to read/write objects such as the customer-master.xlsx file it stores.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects (including sensitive customer data) are stored unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious overwrite/deletion of objects (compounded by force_destroy and public access) cannot be recovered from.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in public unencrypted bucket
findings.description: A sensitive file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded into the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving it unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled for the financials bucket, increasing risk of irrecoverable data loss or tampering, especially combined with force_destroy = true.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the operations bucket, so data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the data_science bucket, leaving stored data unencrypted at rest.
